nouns.explanation: A place with many houses, shops and streets, smaller than a city.
The main street of a town, where most of the shops are.
An open space in the middle of a town where a market is held.
The building from which a town is run.
A tall tower with a large clock on it.
The tall, pointed tower of a church.
A shop where bread and cakes are made and sold.
A place that sells drinks and light meals.
A place where books can be borrowed.
A place where trains or buses stop.
Rows of houses joined together.
The tops of buildings.
The pipes on a roof that carry smoke away.
Narrow little roads.
Rounded stones set in the ground to make an old road.
The path beside a road where people walk.
Cloth roofs over shop fronts that keep off sun and rain.
Tables in a market where goods are sold.
People who sell things.
Things that are for sale.
The people who live near you.
Hollow metal objects that ring when struck.
Long seats for several people.
A factory, especially one that makes cloth.
Strings of small coloured flags.
A tall post with a light on top.
The steps outside front doors.
Thin, flat pieces of grey stone used on roofs.
The opening that a door fits into.
A picture made by cutting lines into metal and printing from it.

adjectives.explanation: Covered with flat pieces of baked clay.
With boards nailed over the windows and doors.
Made black by years of smoke.
Too small, with not enough room.
Full of things in an untidy way.
Worn by wind, rain and sun.
Made smooth or thin by long use.

verbs.explanation: Sat snugly in a sheltered place.
Stood close together in a group.
Crowded close together.
Stood in a row along the side of something.
Went along with many twists and turns.
Went gently downhill or uphill.
Had a view down onto something.
Rang to mark the time.
Rang out loudly and joyfully.
Was full of busy activity.
Chatted about other people's lives.
Walked in a slow, relaxed way.
Stood in a line, waiting.
Sold goods by calling out in the street.
Made a series of quick knocking sounds.
Floated gently through the air, like a smell.
Moved in a twisting, curving shape.
Shone with a soft, warm light.
Made a sound that bounced back so it was heard again.
Cleaned the ground with a brush.
Became empty.
Flew out suddenly.
Flapped lightly and quickly.
Walked with strong, even steps.
Moved slowly and quietly.
Made something vanish, as if eating it.
Pulled something off roughly.
Rushed along out of control.
Floated slowly through the air.
Was full of a loud, clear sound.

nounsAndAdjectives.text: Warm, yeasty smell of fresh bread

sentences.text: The small, sleepy town nestled in the valley, cupped in the green palm of the hills.
Shops and cafés clustered around the square in the shadow of the weathered, stone clock tower.
Shops with faded, striped awnings lined the high street.
Narrow, cobbled streets wound up the hill towards the church, too steep for anything but feet.
The town hall clock chimed the hour, and pigeons burst from the roof like thrown confetti.
On Saturdays the thriving market square bustled with shoppers.
Neighbours gossiped on the doorsteps of the neat, red-brick terraces.
The warm, yeasty smell of fresh bread wafted from the bakery and drew a queue before dawn.
Grey smoke curled from the chimneys and drifted over the crooked, tiled rooftops.
It was a drab, soot-blackened mill town, where rows of cramped houses huddled beneath the factory chimneys.
As darkness fell, lamps glowed in the windows of the picturesque, historic town.
A delivery van rattled over the cobbles before anyone else was awake.
The dilapidated, boarded-up shops had stood empty for years, their signs fading letter by letter.
A row of worn, wooden benches overlooked the river.
Cheerful, chattering shoppers queued at the bus stop, laden with bags.
Traders hawked their wares from behind the colourful market stalls.
His footsteps echoed down the empty street, and every doorway on the dark, deserted high street seemed to shelter a shadow.
The main road sloped down to the station at the foot of the town.
On Sunday afternoons, families strolled through the park and fed the ducks.
Church bells pealed across the rooftops.
Every morning the shopkeeper swept the pavement outside his tiny, cluttered shop.
Quiet, winding lanes led away from the square, between gardens heavy with roses.
She had lived there all her life, and every street was peopled with friendly, familiar faces.
The steamy, crowded café rang with clattering cups and laughter.
Flower baskets hung from every lamp post, and the whole town smelled of summer.
By nine o'clock the streets had emptied, and the town seemed to be holding its breath.
The storm tore slates from the roofs and sent bins careering down the high street.
On carnival day, bunting fluttered above the streets and a brass band marched through the town.
Fog crept in from the river and swallowed the street lamps one by one.
Under a covering of snow, the town looked like an engraving on an old Christmas card.
